restrictions: Messages A and B have 128 bytes each: one chunk of two full blocks, block 0 with flags CHUNK_START and the root block 1 with flags CHUNK_END | ROOT, counter 0 and block length 64. The chaining values after block 0 differ only in word 0, by 1, and block 1 of B differs from block 1 of A only in word m0, by -1.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 1 prefix round, standard IV, chunk structure, flags and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.
Deterministic: the algorithm uses no coins and outputs the same collision on every run, so there is no failed trial and no restart.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; a straight-line program charged with 4 target compressions (the complete hashes of both messages, for the final collision check) and with memory traffic at four primitive operations per data operation.

No preprocessing, table, stored collision or nonuniform advice: every word of the output is computed by the counted program from public constants; the preprocessing and advice fields are zero-valued upper bounds because the schema cannot express log2(0).

Specific to the 1-round prefix: the identities are proved for one round only, nothing is claimed for two or more rounds (the pair has different 2-round digests), and no priority or novelty claim is made.
